000db5b5-a522-44b0-9a6c-658f3f9bae9f: This medicine is used for difficulty in expectorating sputum in acute and chronic bronchitis, bronchial asthma, laryngitis, sinusitis and cystic fibrosis.
For acute conditions, adults take 1 capsule (200 mg) per dose, 3 times a day, and those aged 6 to 14 years take 1 capsule (200 mg) per dose, 2 times a day, before meals with a small amount of water.

For chronic conditions, adults take 1 capsule (200 mg) per dose, 2 times a day, and those aged 6 to 14 years take 1/2 capsule (100 mg) per dose, 3 times a day, before meals with a small amount of water.
For cystic fibrosis, those aged 6 years and older take 1 capsule (200 mg) per dose, 3 times a day, before meals with a small amount of water.

Do not take this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it, or if you have gastric or duodenal ulcer, are an infant under 2 years of age, or have hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.
Before taking this medicine, pregnant women, women who may be pregnant and breast-feeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

If nausea, vomiting, stomatitis, heartburn, diarrhoea, urticaria, itching, rash, headache, tinnitus, bronchospasm (especially in asthmatic patients), tachycardia or hypertension occurs rarely, or anaphylaxis occurs very rarely, immediately stop taking this medicine and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
When taken together with oral antibiotics (amoxicillin, cefuroxime, doxycycline, erythromycin, thiamphenicol), take them at least 2 hours apart.
Store out of the reach of children.
002063d6-2bea-4975-9fab-7d13bba0a19f: This medicine is used for the temporary relief of burning, irritation and discomfort caused by dry eye or by exposure to wind and sun, and for the prevention of further eye irritation.
Bend the tip of the container fully back and forth, then pull it off to open.
When necessary, instill 1 to 2 drops into the affected eye; after instillation, discard the remaining solution and the container.
Do not use the solution if it has changed colour or become cloudy.
If this medicine is swallowed by accident, get professional help immediately.
Do not reuse after a single use; be sure to discard the remaining solution and the container.
To avoid contamination, do not let the tip of the container touch any surface.

If you experience pain, changes in vision, continued redness or irritation, or if the condition worsens or persists for more than 72 hours, immediately stop using this medicine and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Store out of the reach of children.
000eb144-db87-4d29-bcfa-dad852a15c3c: This medicine is used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, chills (feeling cold and shivering), fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
Adults take 1 bottle per dose, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.
Leave an interval of 4 hours between doses.
Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it, if you have experienced asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, if you are an infant under 2 years of age, or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinsonian agent, etc.) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has or is suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, if you have an allergic constitution, if you have experienced allergic symptoms caused by medicines (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching), or if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, hypertension, swelling, gastric or duodenal ulcer, if you are elderly or in a weakened condition, or if you have high fever, heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain, ulcer or bleeding problems, or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.
If there is no improvement in your symptoms after 5 to 6 doses, immediately stop taking this medicine and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported; if a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
Be sure to follow the prescribed dosage and administration.

If rash or redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema (swelling), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia or high anion gap metabolic acidosis occurs, or rarely symptoms of shock (urticaria, swelling or chest tightness immediately after taking, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms such as congested and reddened skin with high fever and burn-like blistering appearing over the whole body skin and on the mouth or eye mucosa), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice, cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever, decreased urine volume or swelling of the face, hands and feet, heaviness of the eyelids, stiffening of the hands, increased blood pressure, headache or myopathy (weakness, limb cramps, paralysis) occurs, immediately stop taking this medicine and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine together with antitussive-expectorants (phlegm medicines), other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness remedies, antiallergic medicines) or flucloxacillin.

Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine together with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, potassium-containing preparations, liquorice-containing preparations, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, etacrynic acid) or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide), antidiabetic medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants or steroids.
Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.
Store at room temperature, protected from moisture and light.
Store out of the reach of children.
012903c2-bdfb-474b-861e-042c01c45f4c: This medicine is used for the analgesic and anti-inflammatory relief of stiff shoulders, lower back pain, neuralgia, rheumatism, bruises, sprains, muscle pain and joint pain.
Attach to the affected area 1 to 2 times a day.
Do not use on infants aged 30 months or under, around the eyes, on eczema, on dermatitis caused by lacquer or similar, on wounds or on mucous membranes.
Do not warm the affected area to which the patch is attached with a heater, electric blanket or similar.
Because absorption of a large amount through the skin may cause symptoms of poisoning, avoid long-term use over a wide area.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have experienced allergic symptoms caused by medicines or cosmetics (for example rash, redness, itching or dermatitis caused by lacquer or similar), if you have an allergic constitution, if you have severe moistness or soreness of the skin, or if you are a child, pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.
If there is no improvement in your symptoms after 5 to 6 days of use, immediately stop using this medicine and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
When used for children, use under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
Clean the affected area and wipe off sweat and the like thoroughly before attaching the patch.
Because bathing with the patch attached causes strong irritation, remove it 30 minutes to 1 hour before bathing.
Also, do not attach it immediately after bathing.
Use this medicine for external use only.
Be sure to follow the prescribed dosage and administration.
If rash, congested and reddened skin, itching or pain occurs, immediately stop using this medicine and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Store at room temperature, protected from moisture and light.
Store out of the reach of children.
008c149e-b312-404a-922b-5c2ec1dec0ed: This medicine is used for insect bites, itching and chilblains (frostbite sores).
Attach 1 patch to the affected area (diseased area) 1 to several times (a number of times) a day.

Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it, on children aged 30 months or under, in or around the eyes, on mucous membranes, on eczema, on dermatitis caused by lacquer or similar, on wounds, or on sensitive skin.
Use this medicine for external use only; do not take it by mouth or inhale it.
Do not wrap or bandage the site of application, and do not expose it to external heat or hot water.
Patients with particularly weak skin should not use this medicine continuously on the same area.
Attach for about 4 to 5 hours per application, and do not use on the same area for a long time.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have ever had allergic symptoms caused by medicines or cosmetics, if you have an allergic constitution, or if you have severe moistness, soreness or inflammation of the skin.
If there is no improvement in your symptoms after 5 to 6 days of use, immediately stop using this medicine and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Be sure to follow the prescribed dosage and administration.
When administered to children, administer under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
Take care that it does not get into the eyes; if it does, wash it out with water immediately.
If water touches the area where this medicine has been used, you may feel strong irritation.
If the affected area is wet with sweat or the like, wipe it thoroughly before use.
If rash or redness, swelling, itching, pain or oedema occurs from the use of this medicine, immediately stop using it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Store at room temperature, protected from moisture and light.
Store out of the reach of children.
0181e3ea-a445-407f-a647-b92d5eb4c479: This medicine is used to relieve inflammation caused by dentures (false teeth), oral candidal infections such as thrush, gingivitis, pharyngitis and aphthous stomatitis, and for sterilisation and disinfection after periodontal membrane surgery.
Rinse or gargle the mouth for about 1 minute with 15 mL per dose, 2 times a day, and then spit it out; use after brushing the teeth.
Avoid rinsing with water or another mouthwash, brushing the teeth or eating immediately after use.
In the case of denture-related stomatitis, soak and clean the dentures for 15 minutes, 2 times a day.
The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
Do not use for a long period, as it may cause an imbalance of the normal bacterial flora in the mouth.
Do not use this medicine if you have experienced hypersensitivity to it.
Use for rinsing the mouth only; do not use it for internal use.
Patients who have asthma or another allergic disease, or who have such a history or family history, and pregnant women, breast-feeding women and children should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Temporary parotitis, increased staining of the teeth or the surface of the oral cavity (inside of the mouth), increased formation of supragingival calculus and changes in taste sensation may occur.

If symptoms of shock (for example nausea, discomfort, cold sweat, dizziness, chest tightness, difficulty breathing or convulsions) occur rarely, or rash or urticaria occurs occasionally, immediately stop using this medicine and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Store at room temperature, protected from moisture and light.
Store out of the reach of children.
04a5c6eb-9f30-4928-93a0-09510d806a6f: This medicine is used for the sterilisation and disinfection of cuts, wounds and grazed wound surfaces, and, in the case of haemorrhoids, for the sterilisation and disinfection of the anus.
Spray on the affected area (diseased area) several times (a number of times) a day, or soak gauze or absorbent cotton with it and apply.
Use this medicine for external use only; do not take it by mouth.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have experienced allergic reactions caused by medicines or cosmetics (rash, redness, itching, dermatitis caused by lacquer or similar, etc.), if you have an allergic constitution, if the affected area is extensive, or if the wound or burn is severe.
If there is no improvement in your symptoms after 5 to 6 days of use, immediately stop using this medicine and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Be sure to follow the prescribed dosage and administration.
When administered to children, administer under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
Take care that it does not get into the eyes; if it does, wash it out with water immediately.
If rash, redness, itching or oedema occurs, immediately stop using this medicine and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Store at room temperature, protected from moisture and light.
Store out of the reach of children.
004eb9d6-9378-43fb-9d22-6f232e57d7c3: This medicine is used for candidal vaginitis, trichomonal vaginitis, vaginitis due to non-specific and mixed infections, and preoperative preparation in obstetrics and gynaecology.
Insert 1 tablet (200 mg) deep into the vagina 1 time a day.
It is preferable to insert it in the evening before going to bed.
The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.

Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it, if you have thyroid dysfunction (especially nodular goitre, endemic goitre, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, etc.), renal failure, if you are a newborn or an infant under 6 months of age, if you have dermatitis herpetiformis, or if you are a patient before or after radioactive iodine treatment.
Do not use for ophthalmic or internal use.
Do not use mixed with other preparations.
When used on severe wounds, use distilled water for injection or sterile purified water as the diluent; do not use tap water or purified water.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are severely ill (for example a burn patient), if you have thyroid disease, if you have experienced renal failure, or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.
Take care that it does not get into the eyes; if it does, wash it out with clean water immediately.
Wash and disinfect the affected area thoroughly.
Because soaps weaken the bactericidal action of this medicine, wash them off thoroughly before use.
Take care, as this medicine may weaken latex or rubber products such as condoms and vaginal contraceptive diaphragms.

If anaphylactoid symptoms (difficulty breathing, flushing, urticaria, etc.) or iodine eruption occur rarely, pain, itching, irritation, rash, redness or dermatitis occur occasionally, or burning sensation, skin ulcer, contact dermatitis or skin discoloration occurs rarely, immediately stop using this medicine and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
For other details, please check the detailed information of the marketing authorisation.
Do not use together with hydrogen peroxide.

Consult a doctor or pharmacist when using this medicine together with lithium preparations, chlorhexidine, silver sulfadiazine, alkalis, mercury-containing preparations or enzyme-based wound healing agents.
Store at room temperature, protected from light.
042bd399-345f-4031-8f65-d56f069566d8: This medicine is used to relieve dryness of the nasal mucosa.
For children under 2 years of age, spray 1 time into each nostril.
For children aged 2 years and over, spray 1 to 2 times into each nostril, 2 to 4 times a day or whenever necessary.
Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it or to benzalkonium chloride.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have experienced allergic symptoms related to nasal drops (for example rash, redness, swelling or irritation), if you have recently had nasal surgery, or if you have any change in your body caused by illness.
Use this medicine for nasal instillation only.
For reasons of hygiene, one product should be used by one person only.
Store at room temperature, protected from heat.
Do not use the product after the expiry date.
Store out of the reach of children.
0387c0ed-2c19-4beb-a618-742d91e60f06: This medicine is used to remove intestinal foam during gastroscopy, to remove intestinal gas during abdominal X-ray examination, and to improve abdominal symptoms caused by gas in the gastrointestinal tract (abdominal bloating, aerophagia, etc.).

For adults: to remove intestinal foam during gastroscopy, chew and take 1 tablet per dose 15 to 40 minutes before the examination; to remove intestinal gas during abdominal X-ray examination, chew and take 1 tablet per dose, 3 times a day, after meals or between meals, from 3 to 4 days before the examination; to improve abdominal symptoms caused by gas in the gastrointestinal tract, chew and take 1 tablet per dose, 3 times a day, after meals or at bedtime.
Occasionally loose stools, abdominal discomfort, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, vomiting, nausea, a feeling of abdominal heaviness or loss of appetite, and rarely headache, may occur.
Store at room temperature, protected from moisture and light.
Store out of the reach of children.
019254d1-a2eb-4adb-83a6-c7945d719849: This medicine is used for drug poisoning.
Adults take 50 to 100 mg per dose, 1 to 3 times a day.
The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
If rash, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting or stomach pain occurs rarely, immediately stop taking this medicine and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Store out of the reach of children.
fffd2a52-0a34-408d-8bcd-ac9664759f93: This medicine is used to supply vitamins B1, B2, B6, E and C in cases of physical fatigue, during pregnancy and breast-feeding, when physical strength is reduced during or after illness (during an illness or after recovery), and in old age (when cod liver oil and vitamins D and E are contained), and to relieve the symptoms of neuralgia, muscle pain and joint pain (lower back pain, stiff shoulders, etc.), beriberi and eye fatigue.
Adults take 1 tablet per dose, 2 times a day.

Do not take this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it, if you are a nursing infant under 3 months of age, or if you have hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have hyperoxaluria (a condition in which an excessive amount of oxalate is excreted in the urine), if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, if you are breast-feeding, if you are a premature baby or an infant, if you have gout or kidney stones, if you are deficient in folic acid, if you have a thrombotic predisposition, or if you are hypersensitive to or have experienced hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5.
Be sure to follow the prescribed dosage and administration.
It may interfere with the detection of glucose in various urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, thereby affecting clinical test values.

If stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, constipation, rash, redness, nausea, vomiting, loose stools, stomatitis (inflammation inside the mouth), loss of appetite or abdominal bloating occurs, or if menstruation comes earlier than expected or the flow gradually increases and bleeding continues for a long time, immediately stop taking this medicine and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Do not take this medicine together with levodopa.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine together with oral contraceptives containing oestrogen.
Store at room temperature, protected from moisture and light.
Store out of the reach of children.
18745211-0b92-42b7-974a-e91c87a904ca: This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), fever and pain due to a cold, lower back pain, dysmenorrhoea, postoperative pain, ankylosing spondylitis, headache, toothache, muscle pain, neuralgia, acute gout, psoriatic arthritis, soft tissue injury (sprain, contusion) and non-articular rheumatic disease (tendinitis, tenosynovitis, bursitis).

For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout and psoriatic arthritis, adults take 200-600 mg per dose, 3 to 4 times a day.
Up to a maximum of 3,200 mg may be taken per day.
For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, take 30 to 40 mg per kg of body weight (kg) per dose, in 3 to 4 divided doses a day.
For mild to moderate pain and for a cold, adults take 200 to 400 mg per dose, 3 to 4 times a day.
The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.

For children, those aged 11 to 14 years take 200 to 250 mg (10 to 12.5 mL) per dose, those aged 7 to 10 years take 150 to 200 mg (7.5 to 10 mL) per dose, those aged 3 to 6 years take 100 to 150 mg (5 to 7.5 mL) per dose and those aged 1 to 2 years take 50 to 100 mg (2.5 to 5 mL) per dose, 3 to 4 times a day, and it is preferable to avoid taking it on an empty stomach.

For children, those aged 11 to 14 years may take up to 1,000 mg (50 mL) a day, those aged 7 to 10 years up to 800 mg (40 mL), those aged 3 to 6 years up to 600 mg (30 mL) and those aged 1 to 2 years up to 400 mg (20 mL).

Do not take this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it, or if you have gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, a severe blood disorder, severe hepatic impairment, severe renal impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency, severe hypertension, bronchial asthma, asthma caused by aspirin or other anti-inflammatory analgesics, urticaria, experience of an allergic reaction, pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass surgery, if you are a pregnant woman in the last 3 months of pregnancy, a breast-feeding woman, a patient receiving high-dose methotrexate as chemotherapy, or a patient with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.
Do not take more than the recommended dose.
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.

Patients with uncontrolled hypertension, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease should avoid taking high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day), and patients with cardiovascular risk factors (hypertension, hyperlipidaemia, diabetes, smoking, etc.) should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine if high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) is required.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have a blood disorder, a bleeding tendency, liver cirrhosis, hepatic impairment, renal impairment, cardiac insufficiency, heart disease, hypertension, systemic lupus erythematosus, mixed connective tissue disease, ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, if you are elderly, a child under 2 years of age, pregnant, or a patient with chickenpox.

When taken for a cold, take it in principle for no more than 5 days; without the instruction of a doctor or pharmacist, do not take it for more than 10 days (adults) or more than 5 days (children) for pain, and do not take it for more than 3 days for fever.
It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic reactions, myocardial infarction and stroke, which may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

If shock (difficulty breathing, decreased blood pressure, etc.), blood disorders such as decreased haematocrit, decreased haemoglobin, anaemia, aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, impaired platelet function or eosinophilia, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation (a hole), ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, haematemesis, Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, thirst, stomatitis, abdominal bloating, oral ulcer, constipation, black stools, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis, drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms of unknown frequency, angioneurotic oedema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash, exfoliative dermatitis, acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, hepatitis, jaundice, abnormal liver function, hepatic impairment, hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reaction, asthma attack, urticaria, eczema, purpura, visual disturbance, deafness, tinnitus, taste disturbance, dizziness, drowsiness, light-headedness, depression, headache, cerebrovascular accident or nervousness, aseptic meningitis or meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, stiff neck, fever or impaired consciousness, acute renal failure, decreased urination, haematuria, proteinuria, elevated BUN and blood creatinine, hyperkalaemia, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, decreased urine volume, generalised oedema and accompanying shortness of breath, lassitude, Conn's syndrome of unknown frequency, swelling around the eyes, facial swelling, malaise, fever, nosebleed, swelling or peripheral oedema appears, immediately stop taking this medicine and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Do not take this medicine if you are a patient receiving high-dose methotrexate as chemotherapy, or together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics.

Before taking this medicine, patients taking low-dose aspirin, ACE inhibitors, lithium, furosemide and thiazide diuretics, low-dose methotrexate, coumarin anticoagulants (warfarin, etc.) or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Store at room temperature, protected from light.
Store out of the reach of children.
